clark_report.headline: I'm on the Titans at 60%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Jets offense ranks 30th, the Titans defense ranks 9th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Nissan Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, TEN have been playing better lately.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Jets line gives up a sack on 10.0% of dropbacks (30th), and the Titans get home on 7.0% (9th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Titans.

other_side.title: When the Titans have the ball
body: The Titans line gives up a sack on 8.6% of dropbacks (26th), and the Jets get home on 4.2% (31st).
So the Titans have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: NYJ have allowed slightly less on a typical play than TEN this season. That makes it harder for TEN to put together scoring drives.
Two extra possessions for the Jets would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Jets score 14 or more in the first half, the Titans defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Jets win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Seahawks at 82%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Seahawks offense ranks 2nd, the Cardinals defense ranks 29th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest football reason? Over the last three games, SEA have won more often than ARI, and their scoring margin is about 34 points a game better.
On top of that, rest tilts toward SEA.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2025), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Seahawks score 29.2 points a game (2nd in the league), and the Cardinals allow 28.7 (29th).
On a typical play the Seahawks gain 5.6 yards (6th), while the Cardinals give up 5.5 (26th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Seahawks.

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball
body: The Cardinals score 20.9 points a game (22nd in the league), and the Seahawks allow 16.9 (1st).
On a typical play the Cardinals gain 4.8 yards (20th), while the Seahawks give up 4.4 (4th).
So the Seahawks have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Seahawks have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the 49ers at 57%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Levi's Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 6.5 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the offenses have been about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the 49ers gain 7.1 yards (1st), while the Broncos give up 5.3 (22nd).
The 49ers score 32.7 points a game (2nd in the league), and the Broncos allow 23.3 (17th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the 49ers.

other_side.title: When the Broncos have the ball
body: The Broncos score 20.0 points a game (21st in the league), and the 49ers allow 16.7 (3rd).
On a typical play the Broncos gain 4.5 yards (22nd), while the 49ers give up 4.5 (7th).
So the 49ers have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: DEN have been playing better lately.

Two extra possessions for the Broncos would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the 49ers have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Broncos win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bills at 74%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Bills offense ranks 3rd, the Raiders defense ranks 28th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? BUF are 2-1 over their last three games; LV are 1-2. They also have about 10 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, bUF's defense has been tougher.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Bills gain 6.2 yards (3rd), while the Raiders give up 5.5 (28th).
The Bills score 32.8 points a game (1st in the league), and the Raiders allow 25.8 (22nd).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Bills.

other_side.title: When the Raiders have the ball
body: The Raiders score 26.4 points a game (9th in the league), and the Bills allow 28.2 (28th).
The Raiders line gives up a sack on 4.3% of dropbacks (6th), and the Bills get home on 5.1% (23rd).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Raiders, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Raiders are 9th in points per game (26.4). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Raiders would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bills have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Raiders win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bears at 54%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Bears offense ranks 10th, the Falcons defense ranks 22nd. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? Over the last three games, CHI and ATL have gained about the same on a typical play, so offense isn't where this game gets decided.
On top of that, CHI have the better scoring margin.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Bears line gives up a sack on 5.3% of dropbacks (10th), and the Falcons get home on 5.2% (22nd).
The Bears score 23.8 points a game (13th in the league), and the Falcons allow 24.4 (21st).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Bears.

other_side.title: When the Falcons have the ball
body: On a typical play the Falcons gain 5.7 yards (6th), while the Bears give up 5.5 (27th).
The Falcons line gives up a sack on 7.1% of dropbacks (23rd), and the Bears get home on 9.2% (2nd).
So the Bears have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Falcons are 6th in yards per play (5.7). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Falcons would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bears have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Falcons win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Browns at 53%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Titans offense ranks 31st, the Browns defense ranks 7th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest football reason? CLE are 2-1 over their last three games; TEN are 1-2. They also have about 8 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Titans score 14.0 points a game (31st in the league), and the Browns allow 20.3 (7th).
On a typical play the Titans gain 4.2 yards (29th), while the Browns give up 4.7 (9th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Browns.

other_side.title: When the Browns have the ball
body: The Browns line gives up a sack on 10.8% of dropbacks (32nd), and the Titans get home on 7.0% (11th).
The Browns score 17.7 points a game (28th in the league), and the Titans allow 21.5 (13th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Titans, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: The defenses have been about even.
items.text: CLE's defense has actually allowed less per play over the last three games, so defense isn't a real edge for TEN in this game.
Two extra possessions for the Titans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Titans score 14 or more in the first half, the Browns defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Titans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 53% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Browns win about 53 of them. That means the Titans win 47, which is a lot.

line.body: The line has the Browns by 2.5, about 54%. I'm at 53%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: This is the part working against my pick: injuries pull my number about 4.7 points toward the Titans.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Titans win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Cardinals offense ranks 24th, the Broncos defense ranks 10th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest football reason? DEN are 2-1 over their last three games; ARI are 1-2. They also have about 11 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, DEN are the healthier team this week.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Cardinals score 21.0 points a game (24th in the league), and the Broncos allow 20.8 (10th).
On a typical play the Cardinals gain 4.3 yards (27th), while the Broncos give up 4.9 (14th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Broncos.

other_side.title: When the Broncos have the ball
body: The Broncos line gives up a sack on 4.2% of dropbacks (6th), and the Cardinals get home on 6.9% (13th).
So the Broncos have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: The defenses have been about even.
items.text: DEN's defense has actually allowed less per play over the last three games, so defense isn't a real edge for ARI in this game.
Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Cardinals score 14 or more in the first half, the Broncos defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 67% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Broncos win about 67 of them. That means the Cardinals win 33, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Broncos by 4.5, about 67%. I'm at 67%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: The injury report pushes me about 1.3 points further toward the Broncos. The Broncos are the healthier team this week.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Cardinals win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Rams at 73%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Chargers offense ranks 30th, the Rams defense ranks 5th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest football reason? The game is at SoFi Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, LA have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Chargers gain 4.2 yards (30th), while the Rams give up 4.4 (5th).
The Chargers score 15.0 points a game (30th in the league), and the Rams allow 23.0 (17th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Rams.

other_side.title: When the Rams have the ball
body: On a typical play the Rams gain 5.6 yards (6th), while the Chargers give up 5.1 (19th).
The Rams line gives up a sack on 3.6% of dropbacks (5th), and the Chargers get home on 6.1% (18th).
So the Rams have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Chargers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Chargers score 14 or more in the first half, the Rams defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Chargers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 73% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Rams win about 73 of them. That means the Chargers win 27, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Rams by 7, about 72%. I'm at 73%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Chargers win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.

On top of that, KC are at home.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 6.5 yards (1st), while the Cardinals give up 5.6 (30th).
The Chiefs score 28.0 points a game (5th in the league), and the Cardinals allow 29.7 (31st).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Chiefs.

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball
body: On a typical play the Cardinals gain 4.3 yards (27th), while the Chiefs give up 4.3 (3rd).
The Cardinals score 21.0 points a game (24th in the league), and the Chiefs allow 16.6 (2nd).
So the Chiefs have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: The defenses have been about even.
items.text: KC's defense has actually allowed less per play over the last three games, so defense isn't a real edge for ARI in this game.
Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Chiefs have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 58% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Chiefs win about 58 of them. That means the Cardinals win 42, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Cardinals win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Jets at 50%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Dolphins offense ranks 31st, the Jets defense ranks 5th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? NYJ are 1-2 over their last three games; MIA are 0-3. They also have about 4 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, division game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Dolphins score 14.0 points a game (31st in the league), and the Jets allow 20.3 (5th).
The Dolphins line gives up a sack on 9.3% of dropbacks (29th), and the Jets get home on 7.3% (10th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Jets.

other_side.title: When the Jets have the ball
body: On a typical play the Jets gain 4.6 yards (21st), while the Dolphins give up 5.5 (26th).
So the Jets have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.text: Two extra possessions for the Dolphins would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Dolphins score 14 or more in the first half, the Jets defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Dolphins win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 50% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Jets win about 50 of them. That means the Dolphins win 50, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Dolphins win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

change_my_mind: If the Bears have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Jaguars win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

meaning.title: What 55% actually means

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Jaguars win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

change_my_mind: If the Commanders score 14 or more in the first half, the Titans defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Commanders win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 53% actually means

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.

body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 6.5 yards (1st), while the Patriots give up 5.0 (18th).

other_side.title: When the Patriots have the ball

On paper this side of the ball is a wash, so I'm not leaning on it either way.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

If the Patriots win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bills at 52%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Bills offense ranks 3rd, the Broncos defense ranks 14th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? Both teams are 2-1 over their last three, so the records are even. The difference is scoring margin: BUF have about 1 more point of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, the defenses have been about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Bills gain 6.0 yards (3rd), while the Broncos give up 4.9 (14th).
The Bills line gives up a sack on 6.0% of dropbacks (19th), and the Broncos get home on 7.4% (8th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Bills.

other_side.title: When the Broncos have the ball
body: The Broncos line gives up a sack on 4.2% of dropbacks (6th), and the Bills get home on 4.3% (26th).
On a typical play the Broncos gain 4.0 yards (32nd), while the Bills give up 5.2 (21st).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Broncos, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Broncos are 10th in points allowed per game (20.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Broncos would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bills have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Broncos win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 52% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Bills win about 52 of them. That means the Broncos win 48, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Broncos win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Cowboys at 53%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Cowboys offense ranks 2nd, the Jaguars defense ranks 22nd. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? The game is at AT&T Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the defenses have been about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Cowboys line gives up a sack on 2.6% of dropbacks (2nd), and the Jaguars get home on 5.1% (22nd).
On a typical play the Cowboys gain 5.1 yards (13th), while the Jaguars give up 5.3 (23rd).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Cowboys.

other_side.title: When the Jaguars have the ball
body: On a typical play the Jaguars gain 5.3 yards (11th), while the Cowboys give up 5.6 (31st).
The Jaguars score 25.7 points a game (9th in the league), and the Cowboys allow 26.5 (25th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Jaguars, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: JAX have been playing better lately.
items.text: JAX are 2-1 over their last three games; DAL are 1-2. They also have about 6 more points of scoring margin per game.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Jaguars are 3rd in points allowed per game (17.3). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Jaguars would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Cowboys have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Jaguars win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 53% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Cowboys win about 53 of them. That means the Jaguars win 47, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Jaguars win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bears at 52%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Bears offense ranks 8th, the Lions defense ranks 30th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Soldier Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the offenses have been about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Bears score 25.7 points a game (8th in the league), and the Lions allow 29.6 (30th).
The Bears line gives up a sack on 6.3% of dropbacks (20th), and the Lions get home on 8.0% (4th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Bears.

other_side.title: When the Lions have the ball
body: On a typical play the Lions gain 5.6 yards (5th), while the Bears give up 5.5 (29th).
The Lions line gives up a sack on 5.6% of dropbacks (15th), and the Bears get home on 9.1% (2nd).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Lions, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: The defenses have been about even.
items.text: CHI's defense has actually allowed less per play over the last three games, so defense isn't a real edge for DET in this game.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Lions are 2nd in points per game (32.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Lions would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bears have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Lions win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 52% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Bears win about 52 of them. That means the Lions win 48, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Lions win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Saints at 53%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Saints offense ranks 9th, the Buccaneers defense ranks 25th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Caesars Superdome. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the defenses have been about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Saints line gives up a sack on 4.6% of dropbacks (9th), and the Buccaneers get home on 4.5% (25th).
On a typical play the Saints gain 4.3 yards (25th), while the Buccaneers give up 4.8 (11th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Saints.

other_side.title: When the Buccaneers have the ball
body: The Buccaneers line gives up a sack on 8.8% of dropbacks (27th), and the Saints get home on 6.3% (17th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Buccaneers, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Buccaneers are 11th in yards per play allowed (4.8). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.
Two extra possessions for the Buccaneers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Saints have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Buccaneers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 53% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Saints win about 53 of them. That means the Buccaneers win 47, which is a lot.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Buccaneers win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.
